suggestions.reason: This assertion enumerates specific unchanged items but doesn't cover docs/contracts/ddl.sql, which this run DID modify (added 'UNIQUE' plus a two-line comment to tickets.slug). The skill's own P5-contract-extraction reference defines ddl.sql as a verbatim, frozen dump of the LEGACY schema used mechanically by census.py — not a place to encode target/modern behavior. This run's edit is well-intentioned (it documents the ruling at the point closest to the schema) but is a genuine contract-freeze violation the current assertion set does not catch, since it only names WO-001/PB-001/PB-002/legacy_ref. Consider adding an explicit assertion that docs/contracts/ddl.sql is unchanged (or, if a target-schema location exists elsewhere in the workspace convention, that the UNIQUE constraint lands there instead).

This run's final_report.md states outright that it 'read the actual render_guide.py logic' to hand-sync guide/decisions.md and guide/then-vs-now.md. That script does not exist anywhere inside the ticketd-rewrite-root workspace (fixture) that this baseline was scoped to — it exists only at ../rebuild-kit/scripts/render_guide.py, the actual skill's implementation, which sits as a sibling directory of rebuild-kit-workspace on disk. I copied the output workspace and literally re-ran that exact script against it: the result was byte-for-byte identical to what the executor hand-wrote, including generator-specific formatting quirks (the exact pipe-table layout, the 'moved from Still-open bucket using the literal string (none) vs (none yet)' distinction) that would be very hard to reproduce by convention-guessing alone. This is strong evidence the 'without_skill' baseline discovered and read the skill's real script via ordinary filesystem exploration, despite not being told about the skill or given its path. If the intent of the without_skill arm is to measure genuinely unaided behavior, this run is contaminated: it benefited from the skill's exact rendering logic without following the skill's SKILL.md protocol (e.g. it did not actually invoke render_guide.py as a tool, which the skill's own workflow would have done, and it may not have absorbed the skill's other conventions, like the ddl.sql contract-freeze rule it then violated). Recommend either sandboxing without_skill runs so the sibling skill directory is not filesystem-reachable, or explicitly flagging this run's guide-layer assertion result as unreliable evidence of no-skill capability.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 assertions pass on genuine evidence — this was a well-executed, minimal patch that correctly threaded the ruling through open-questions.md, WO-002, PB-003, ledger.json, the divergence manifest, and the guide layer, and a real re-run of the skill's own render_guide.py against the output reproduced the hand-synced guide files byte-for-byte. Two concerns to weigh alongside the pass rate: (1) CONTAMINATION — the run's own final_report.md admits it read render_guide.py's actual source to hand-sync the guide, and that script only exists in the sibling skill directory, not in the scoped workspace; the byte-for-byte reproduction I verified independently corroborates that it really did read (or effectively reconstruct with implausible precision) the skill's real logic, which undermines this arm's value as a 'no skill' baseline. (2) CONTRACT-FREEZE — the run added a UNIQUE constraint to docs/contracts/ddl.sql, a file the skill's own P5 reference defines as a verbatim, frozen dump of the LEGACY schema (not the migration target), and which census.py consumes mechanically; no assertion currently checks this file, so the violation passed unnoticed.
